graph_titles.title: Tertiary educational attainment by sex, Persons aged 25-34 with a tertiary educational attainment level

national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education. Tertiary education covers short-cycle tertiary education, bachelor's, master's and doctoral studies, corresponding to ISCED 2011 levels 5–8.
national_rationale: The data source is the Labour Force Survey conducted by the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina (BHAS). Data are collected annually, and the educational attainment of respondents is classified in accordance with the International Standard Classification of Education, ISCED 2011. The indicator is expressed as the percentage of the population aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education. Progress is monitored based on changes in the indicator value over time, with an increase in the share indicating progress.
natioanal_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers the population of Bosnia and Herzegovina aged 25 to 34 who have completed one of the levels of tertiary education, from short-cycle tertiary education to doctoral studies (ISCED 5–8). The indicator definition and education classification are aligned with the EU methodological framework, allowing comparisons between data for Bosnia and Herzegovina and those for EU Member States and other European countries. When analysing time series, changes in the Labour Force Survey methodology and the break in the series from 2021, when the new methodological framework was introduced, should be taken into account.
national_long_objective: Modernisation and increased inclusiveness of higher education, together with a gradual increase in the university completion rate, with the aim of moving closer to the EU average. No specific quantified national target has been established for the share of the population aged 25 to 34 with completed tertiary education. The European Union's 2030 target serves as a reference framework for monitoring and comparison and does not constitute a formally established national target for Bosnia and Herzegovina.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the population aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education. Tertiary education covers short-cycle tertiary education, bachelor's, master's and doctoral studies, corresponding to ISCED 2011 levels 5–8. Data up to 2013 are based on ISCED 1997, which covers levels 5–6. ISCED (International Standard Classification of Education) 2011 levels 5–8 for data from 2014 onwards and to ISCED 1997 levels 5–6 for data up to 2013. The indicator is based on the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS).
eu_rationale: The data are obtained from the European Statistical System (ESS) and are based on the European Union Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Data are collected annually and expressed as the share of the population aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education. Eurostat processes and publishes the data in accordance with the EU-LFS methodological framework.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers the population aged 25 to 34 who have completed one of the levels of tertiary education, from short-cycle tertiary education to doctoral studies. The data allow changes to be monitored over time and comparisons to be made between countries. When interpreting time series, breaks in the series in 2014, due to the transition to ISCED 2011, and in 2021, due to the implementation of the new EU-LFS methodological framework, should be taken into account.
eu_long_objective: Tertiary education contributes to the development of knowledge and skills, employability, productivity, innovation and competitiveness. Educational attainment is also linked to opportunities for labour market participation and to reducing the risk of poverty and social exclusion. Under the Strategic Framework for European Cooperation in Education and Training for the period 2026–2030, the target is for at least 47% of the EU population aged 25 to 34 to have attained tertiary education by 2030. This target represents a collective EU reference level and is not an individual target for each Member State.
